title: Ways to Read a Digit Code
statement:
A message of capital letters was turned into digits with A → 1, B → 2, …, Z → 26, and the numbers were written one after another with no separators. You get the digit string s.

Return in how many ways s can be cut back into letters. Each piece must be a number from 1 to 26 written without a leading zero: "0" and "07" are not valid pieces. If no reading exists, return 0.

The count can be huge, so return it modulo 1 000 000 007.

examples.why: The 0 must pair with the 2 before it as 20, which forces 1·20·3. Reading 12 first strands the 0.
30 is above 26 and a lone 0 is not a letter, so the 0 has nothing to join. Counting digit pairs ≤ 26 without these checks gets this wrong.

hints: Look at the end of the string. The last letter came from either the last digit alone or the last two digits together.
Let ways(i) be the number of readings of the first i digits. The last digit alone is valid when it is not 0; the last two together are valid when they form 10..26.
ways(i) = (s[i−1] ≠ '0' ? ways(i−1) : 0) + (s[i−2..i−1] in 10..26 ? ways(i−2) : 0), with ways(0) = 1. Keep two variables and take the modulo at every step.

explain.intuition:
This is the staircase count with conditions on each move. Reading the string from the left, each "move" eats one digit or two, but a move is only allowed if what it eats is a valid letter code.

State: ways(i) = number of readings of the prefix s[0..i−1] (the first i digits). Recurrence: split by the last piece. If it is one digit, it must not be 0, and the rest is any reading of the first i − 1 digits. If it is two digits, they must form a number from 10 to 26 (which also rules out a leading 0), and the rest is any reading of the first i − 2. Base: ways(0) = 1, the empty reading. Fill left to right, keep two values, and reduce modulo 10⁹ + 7 so the numbers stay small.
steps: State: ways(i) = readings of the first i digits. Base: ways(0) = 1.
Two-digit piece: if i ≥ 2 and 10 ≤ int(s[i−2..i−1]) ≤ 26, add ways(i−2).
Take the sum modulo 1 000 000 007, and slide the two variables forward.
pitfalls: Treating "0" as a valid single piece. Every string with a 0 then gets readings it does not have; "301" must be 0.
Accepting two-digit pieces like "05" because 5 ≤ 26. Check the range 10..26, not just ≤ 26.
Starting with ways(0) = 0. Then nothing is ever counted. The empty prefix has exactly one reading: no letters.

solutions.title: Plain recursion
solutions.idea: From position i, try a one-digit piece and a two-digit piece and recurse on the rest. No cache, so exponential.

solutions.title: Table over prefixes
solutions.idea: ways[i] for every prefix length, filled left to right from ways[0] = 1.

solutions.title: Two rolling variables
solutions.idea: Only ways(i − 1) and ways(i − 2) are read, so keep two numbers.

followups: The string may also contain *, which stands for any digit 1–9. How does the recurrence change?
Return one valid reading as letters, or all of them for a short string.
